metadata.title: Nvidia taps Heidrick & Struggles to lead CEO search, WSJ reports

content.text:
Investing.com -- NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) has retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to spearhead the recruitment of its next chief executive officer, according to a report from The Wall Street Journal. The mandate initiates a formal succession process as the chipmaker navigates an abrupt leadership transition following the departure of co-founder Jensen Huang.
Jeff Sanders, co-managing partner of Heidrick's global CEO and board directors practice, is leading the search, people familiar with the matter told the Journal. The firm has already begun engaging prospective external contenders, including Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas, while Nvidia evaluates a pool of both internal and outside candidates.
The search comes in the wake of Huang's resignation earlier this month amid disclosures of extramarital affairs, including relationships with an employee and a suspected Chinese spy. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has stepped in as interim chief executive to maintain operational continuity during the transition.
Despite calls from several technology executives and some Nvidia employees to reinstate Huang, the company's board is not considering bringing him back, the Journal reported. Huang stated on Tuesday, in his first public remarks since exiting the company, that he would be willing to return if asked by the board.
Alongside the executive search, Nvidia's directors have enlisted law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an independent inquiry into the fallout from Huang's conduct. The investigation focuses on whether any corporate or national security secrets were compromised, underscoring the heightened governance and regulatory scrutiny surrounding the chipmaker.
